This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.317/2022 dated 28.11.2022 registered at Police Station- Orchha Road, District- Chhatarpur, for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 370,
372, 373, 376, 376(3), 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 5L/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

sentences.text: applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.

He further submits that the prosecutrix and her parents have been examined before the trial Court and they have turned hostile,
did not support the prosecution story.
He submits that the applicant undertakes to cooperate in trial as well as investigation and would make himself available as and when required.
Trial will take considerable time to conclude.
Upon these submissions, learned counsel prays that the applicant may be released on bail.
On the contrary, learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State opposes the bail application.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case-diary.
According to the prosecution case, 16 years old prosecutrix was missing on 11.09.2022 and recovered on 02.02.2023.
In this period of almost 5 months, she was not only sexually abused but also allegedly sold by persons involved in the crime.

According to the school record, date of birth of the prosecutrix was 20.08.2007 and in her statements recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., she has very clearly stated about the act of present applicant.
Looking to the nature of crime committed by the applicant, this Court is not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application stands rejected.

(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE Prachi Jaggu @ Jagmohan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119236726/
